title: What If Every Deer in America Vanished Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if every deer in America vanished? The roads would change first. The forests, later.
In the early 1900s only about 500,000 white-tailed deer were left. Today it's 25 to 30 million.
They cause roughly 440 deaths and 59,000 injuries a year in collisions, and one 2003 estimate counted 1.5 million crashes.
Deer eat red oak, sugar maple and white ash seedlings, which changes which trees grow back.
At one New York park, a no-hunting area of 1,200 acres had no saplings or underbrush left.
Timber damage alone is estimated at $750 million a year. Without deer, young forests would finally get a chance.

description:
What if every deer in America vanished?
Fewer crashes, and forests that browsing has stripped could regrow.
